learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences
Develop interpersonal skills
Develop the ability to work in a team
Ability to apply knowledge to practice
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training
Ability to work autonomously
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering, for the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section
Ability to exercise teaching in the terms required by current regulations.
Describe the important points and zones of the conventional tensile test curve.
Justify the use of the yield curve in plastic deformation.
Obtain the yield curve from the conventional tensile test curve.
Demonstrate that the true strain is the sum of the partial strains.
Justify the improvement of properties of plastically deformed materials.
Enumerate the objectives pursued with plastic deformation procedures.
Classify deformation procedures based on the temperature used.
Briefly describe hot deformation.
Enumerate the advantages of hot deformation over cold deformation.
Enumerate the disadvantages of hot deformation.
Briefly describe the influence exerted by the deformation speed.
Briefly describe the forging process.
Classify forging procedures based on the tool used.
Calculate stresses and strains in forging.
Briefly describe the rolling process.
Describe the transformations a billet undergoes to become a finished product.
Explain the different types of rolling mills.
Enumerate the causes that produce thickness variation in the rolled product.
Write the expression that must be met in rolling for self-feeding of the material.
Design plate rolling processes based on machine characteristics and material used.
Briefly describe the drawing process.
Briefly describe the parts of a die.
Explain why the drawing stress must be lower than the material's yield stress.
Demonstrate the maximum theoretical cross-sectional reduction in drawing.
Design drawing processes based on machine characteristics and material used.
Briefly describe the extrusion process.
Differentiate the different types of extrusion.
Design extrusion processes based on machine characteristics and material used.
Briefly explain the heading process.
Briefly explain the maximum length/diameter ratio in heading.
Briefly explain the sheet metal cutting process.
Identify, by means of a drawing, the different zones observed at the edge of a sheet.
Differentiate the terms shearing, punching, and cutting.
Reason the condition that must be met to prevent the punching tool from crushing.
Explain which element the clearance between the punch and the die must be applied to, depending on the operation to be performed.
Formulate the advantages and disadvantages of different ways of arranging parts in blanking.
Calculate the forces produced in cutting and punching operations.
Analyze the fundamental problems of the bending operation.
Precisely define the bending operation.
Calculate developments for obtaining different bent parts.
Calculate the necessary forces for the bending operation.
Briefly describe the deep drawing process.
Enumerate the fundamental differences between a cutting die and a deep drawing die.
Calculate the characteristic parameters of the deep drawing process.
Describe deep drawing defects and their causes.
Briefly describe how axes are positioned in a machine tool.
Enumerate the main parts of a lathe.
Describe the main geometric characteristics of the lathe.
Briefly explain the movements of feed, depth of cut, and cutting speed in turning.
Describe the parts of the lathe bed.
Enumerate the functions performed by the bed.
Describe the geometry of the lathe's main spindle.
Briefly describe the lathe headstock and its internal and external contents.
Briefly explain the function of the mechanical speed variator.
Enumerate the functions of the tailstock.
Briefly explain the functions of the carriages in the lathe.
Explain the function of the reversing mechanism.
Explain the purpose of idler gears in a kinematic chain.
Calculate the feeds produced by kinematic chains.
Describe the fundamental parts of a single-point cutting tool.
Differentiate right and left cutting tools.
Differentiate the main cutting motion from the resultant cutting motion.
Explain the reasons why ISO standards define two systems for measuring cutting angles.
Explain how effective angles differ from sharpening angles, and main cutting edge angles from secondary cutting edge angles.
Describe the planes and angles of the tool-in-hand system.
Explain the movements that must be imparted to the tool to achieve longitudinal and transverse sharpening angles.
Briefly explain the factors on which the tool wedge angles depend.
Differentiate positive angles from negative angles.
Explain how to achieve tool wedge angles on a universal grinder.
Describe the planes and angles of the tool-in-use system.
Explain the purpose of the effective clearance angle in machining.
Explain the influence of the effective rake angle in machining.
Enumerate the functions of the main cutting edge angle in machining.
Describe the influence of the secondary cutting edge angle in machining.
Describe the different types of tool tip truncation.
Describe the purposes of constant-profile tools.
Enumerate the types of constant-profile tools.
Select the geometry of the cutting tool based on the operation to be performed, tool and workpiece material, and cutting conditions.
Enumerate the purposes of the chip breaker.
Synthesize the general approach to machining.
Briefly describe the importance of the workpiece plane in the machining process.
Briefly explain the information contained in the machining process of a part.
Describe the machine characteristics that influence the machining process.
Explain the importance of lot size and part complexity in the selection of the machine to be used.
Explain the approach to be taken when selecting the cutting tool material.
Enumerate the properties that the cutting tool material must possess.
Explain the factors on which cutting tool wear depends.
Order cutting tool materials from lowest to highest hardness.
Enumerate the fundamental alloying elements in high-speed steels.
Enumerate the applications of high-speed steel tools.
Explain the difference in chemical composition between high-speed steels and superior high-speed steels.
Explain the main drawback of metallic carbides.
Order families of metallic carbides in increasing order of toughness.
Briefly explain the application of each family of hard metals.
Briefly explain the purposes of coatings on cutting tools.
Briefly explain the properties of ceramic tools.
Describe the applications and cutting conditions of diamond tools.
Enumerate the factors to consider when predicting the properties that the cutting tool material must possess.
Select the cutting tool material based on the workpiece material, allowances to be removed, and characteristics of the machine used.
Make a drawing representing the zones where tool wear occurs.
Enumerate the causes of cutting tool wear.
Create a graph showing how roughness varies with cutting speed, keeping cutting time constant.
Calculate the maximum depth of cut that can be given to the cutting tool.
Enumerate the machining factors influenced by cutting speed.
Apply Taylor's and Kronenberg's theories to calculate cutting speed.
Determine the constants of Taylor's or Kronenberg's generalized expression through tests.
Describe Denis's method for calculating cutting speed.
Differentiate between minimum cost speed and maximum profit speed.
Calculate minimum cost, maximum production, and maximum profit speeds in operations with constant cutting speed.
Calculate minimum cost, maximum production, and maximum profit revolutions per minute in operations with variable cutting speed.
Reason when to lean towards selecting maximum production speeds and when towards maximum economy speeds.
Briefly describe the machining process.
Enumerate the materials and conditions under which continuous chips are produced.
Enumerate the conditions under which continuous chips with built-up edge are produced.
Enumerate the materials and conditions under which discontinuous chips are produced.
Create a graph showing how roughness varies with cutting speed.
Explain the concept of chip upsetting.
Represent, by means of a graph, the cutting speeds, shear plane speed, and chip sliding speed on the rake face, indicating the relationship between them.
Demonstrate that cutting power is the sum of the power consumed in the shear plane and in the sliding of the chip on the rake face.
Briefly describe how to calculate the feed per revolution of the tool.
Calculate the feed per revolution in roughing and finishing operations.
Briefly describe the operations of cylindrical turning, facing, parting, grooving, and knurling.
Calculate the cutting time in turning operations.
Design the machining process for parts obtained by turning.
Define the standardized terminology used in the evaluation of measurement uncertainty, including the definitions of the different uncertainties.
Describe the measurement methods in dimensional metrology.
Describe the law of propagation of uncertainties.
Define and calculate Type A standard uncertainty.
Define and calculate Type B standard uncertainty.
Define and calculate the uncertainty of an input quantity that is related to more than one source of uncertainty.
Differentiate correlated input quantities from uncorrelated ones.
Calculate the covariance in quantities that exhibit a functional relationship.
Estimate covariance using a series of measurements.
Define and calculate expanded uncertainty.
Understand the conditions that must be met to calculate the coverage factor using the normal distribution or Student's t-distribution.
Describe how to express the result of a measurement.
Briefly describe what the calibration operation consists of and the results obtained.
Briefly explain the physical meaning of a precision measurement.
Explain how, through the measurement of a standard, the uncertainty of measurements made with the measurement method is established.
Briefly explain how an instrument is calibrated across its entire scale.
Briefly describe how the measurement and its uncertainty are established with linear interpolation, common correction, and maximum uncertainty methods.
Calculate the value of the measurement and its uncertainty in indirect measurements.
Determine the expressions for obtaining indirect measurements of radii in cylindrical parts, and of angles and diameters in cones.
Determine the expressions for performing indirect measurements of angles in prismatic parts.
Describe the terminology used in threads.
Describe the characteristics of the metric thread.
Describe the characteristics of the Whitworth and Seller threads.
Perform the calibration of a universal caliper.
Perform the calibration of an external hundredth micrometer.
Measure angles in a prismatic part using rollers.
Measure the pitch diameter and angle of a thread.
Measure the angle of an external cone, check the straightness of the generatrices and the concentricity of a section, using the sine bar.
Measure the angle of an internal cone and the extreme diameters using balls.
Calculate the module, base pitch, pressure angle, and tooth thickness of a spur gear, taking the necessary measurements with a caliper and a gear tooth micrometer.

syllabus_topics: PRACTICAL 6. Measurement of a cylindrical spur gear
teaching_methods: Overall control (final exam for theory and problems)
Practicals (instrument calibration, angle and indirect dimension measurement, uncertainty calculation)
Completion of assignments, reports, dissertations, and evaluation tests
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum score of 40% of the corresponding score is required in each activity, and an overall score higher than 50%. For exceptional evaluation, the assessment consists of Theory (30%) and Exercises (70%), with the same minimum passing scores applied.
